gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the EcoFlow DELTA 3 Plus takes only one extra battery connected directly, and that its advertised 5 kWh needs the 4,096 Wh DELTA Pro 3 Smart Extra Battery. With the DELTA 3 extra battery it tops out at 2,048 Wh, and with the DELTA 2 Max extra battery at 3,072 Wh.
standout_why: I compared against the two pages ChatGPT cited (yourpowersetup.com compare, greenmachineadventures.com RV) and the two top unpaid pages (outagereadyhq.com best for camping, solarwaypoint.com 3-way compare). Greenmachine says 'expand with compatible batteries to as much as 5kWh', outagereadyhq says 'expands to 5 kWh with extra batteries', and solarwaypoint lists 'Expandable Capacity 5,120 Wh'. None of them names which battery gets there or says the unit takes only one. Yourpowersetup says nothing about expansion. Solarwaypoint lists the C1000 Gen 2 solar input as one band, '11–60 V, 14.50 A', and yourpowersetup as '11–60V'. Neither gives Anker's lower 8.2 A limit below 29 V. The rivals already say the C1000 Gen 2 can't add batteries and already give the DELTA 3 Plus solar figures (2 × 500 W, 11–60 V) and the Jackery's DC8020 inputs, so those add nothing new.
decides: This backs ChatGPT's picks but tightens the 'longer trips' advice. If a camper wants about 2 kWh, the only DELTA 3 Plus route is a second 1,024 Wh box, for 2,048 Wh total. The Anker SOLIX S2000 gives 2,010 Wh in one unit for $699.99 on Anker's US store, but Anker lists it as not expandable. Getting past about 3 kWh on the DELTA 3 Plus needs the 4,096 Wh DELTA Pro 3 battery, so its '5 kWh' is not a sensible camping path. The C1000 Gen 2 stays the best all-rounder for one or two panels, as long as the panels run at 29–60 V. Low-voltage panels wired in parallel are held to 8.2 A, which is about 230 W at 28 V.

findings.label: Number of extra batteries supported
findings.value: 1 Smart Extra Battery connected directly to the unit
findings.source_title: EcoFlow DELTA 3 Plus FAQ: Everything You Need to Know (EcoFlow, published 2025/6/7)
findings.note: EcoFlow's words: 'DELTA 3 Plus can only support one Smart Extra Battery connected directly to the unit.' The FAQ is on EcoFlow's Canada site. us.ecoflow.com returned HTTP 429 on three tries, so I couldn't check the US page.

findings.label: Compatible extra batteries
findings.value: DELTA 3 (1,024 Wh), DELTA Pro 3 (4,096 Wh), DELTA 2 (1,024 Wh), DELTA 2 Max (2,048 Wh)
findings.source_title: EcoFlow DELTA 3 Plus FAQ: Everything You Need to Know (EcoFlow, published 2025/6/7)
findings.note: Quoted from EcoFlow's list. The FAQ names the connecting port as 'Extra Battery port (XT150)'.

findings.label: Maximum capacity and how to reach it
findings.value: 5,120 Wh only with 1 × DELTA Pro 3 Smart Extra Battery; 2,048 Wh with a DELTA 3 or DELTA 2 extra battery; 3,072 Wh with a DELTA 2 Max extra battery
findings.source_title: EcoFlow DELTA 3 Plus FAQ: Everything You Need to Know (EcoFlow, published 2025/6/7)
findings.note: EcoFlow's words: '1 x DELTA 3 Plus (1024Wh) + 1 x DELTA Pro 3 Smart Extra Battery (4096Wh) = 5kWh'. My arithmetic for the other options, one battery each: 1,024 + 1,024 = 2,048 Wh; 1,024 + 2,048 = 3,072 Wh.

findings.note: EcoFlow's words: 'two PV ports, each supporting 500W (11V-60V) Max'. Solarwaypoint and yourpowersetup already give this.

findings.source_title: EcoFlow DELTA 3 Plus FAQ: Everything You Need to Know (EcoFlow, published 2025/6/7)

findings.label: Solar input by voltage band
findings.value: 11–28 V: 8.2 A max; 29–60 V: 14.5 A max; 600 W max overall
findings.source_title: Anker SOLIX C1000 Gen 2 Portable Power Station (Anker SOLIX US)
findings.note: Anker's spec reads '11-28v⎓8.2A; 29V-60V⎓14.5A (600W Max)'. My arithmetic: the limit is 8.2 A × panel voltage, so 28 V × 8.2 A ≈ 230 W. Any panel or parallel set operating below 29 V is held under about 230 W, whatever its rating. Higher-voltage panels or panels wired in series (29–60 V) are needed to approach 600 W. The page's diagram legend shows an 'XT60i Input Port'.
